decisions.text: Use scripts/wp_to_hugo.py --force to overwrite Phase 1 placeholder About pages and Phase 2 placeholder Artigos Tech.
Popular Posts PT at /posts-populares/ (slug "posts-populares"), EN at /en/popular-posts/ (slug "popular-posts"). Shared translationKey "popular-posts" so the language switcher pairs them.
content/pt-br/about/index.md keeps slug="sobre" (URL /sobre/, matching Phase 1). EN keeps slug="about" (URL /en/about/). Shared translationKey "about".
Posts Populares (PT) and Popular Posts (EN) sit at weight 15 — between Sobre (10) and Recomendações (20) in the nav order.

userStories.title: Migrate 5 remaining WordPress pages with --force to replace placeholders
userStories.description: As the site owner, I want the final 5 WordPress pages (About PT/EN, Popular Posts PT/EN, Artigos Tech) migrated into Hugo so that every page the live site renders is backed by the real WP content instead of Phase 1/2 placeholders.
acceptanceCriteria: A visitor landing on /sobre/, /en/about/, /posts-populares/, /en/popular-posts/, and /recomendacoes/artigos-tech/ sees real content migrated from the WP pages (185, 193, 226, 237, 1606) and no Phase 1 / Phase 2 placeholder sentence remains on any of them.

scripts/content-completion-manifest.json exists at the repo root and is a JSON array of exactly 5 objects, one per WP page id in {185, 193, 226, 237, 1606}, each carrying id, slug, kind="page", lang, target_path, and (for 226/237/1606) translationKey.

Entry 185 uses slug="sobre", lang="pt-br", target_path="content/pt-br/about/index.md", translationKey="about"; entry 193 uses slug="about", lang="en", target_path="content/en/about/index.md", translationKey="about"; entries 226 and 237 share translationKey="popular-posts" so the language switcher pairs them; entry 1606 uses slug="artigos-tech", lang="pt-br", target_path="content/pt-br/recomendacoes/artigos-tech/_index.md".

Running `python3 scripts/wp_to_hugo.py --manifest scripts/content-completion-manifest.json --force` exits 0 and overwrites the three files that already existed (content/pt-br/about/index.md, content/en/about/index.md, content/pt-br/recomendacoes/artigos-tech/_index.md) while creating the two new leaf-bundle files (content/pt-br/posts-populares/_index.md, content/en/popular-posts/_index.md).

Neither the Phase 1 PT placeholder sentence "Olá — sou o Marcelio" nor the Phase 1 EN placeholder sentence "Hey — I'm Marcelio" remains anywhere under content/pt-br/about/index.md or content/en/about/index.md; both files carry a translationKey front-matter line of value "about".

content/pt-br/about/index.md carries a front-matter line `slug: sobre` so the PT page continues to serve at /sobre/ for URL preservation; content/pt-br/posts-populares/_index.md and content/en/popular-posts/_index.md both carry a translationKey front-matter line of value "popular-posts".

A full `hugo --quiet` build from the repo root succeeds and writes public/sobre/index.html, public/en/about/index.html, public/posts-populares/index.html, and public/en/popular-posts/index.html, proving every migrated page renders through the live theme.
`python3 -m py_compile scripts/wp_to_hugo.py` succeeds — the manifest-driven migration path remains syntactically valid Python.
userStories.notes: wp_to_hugo.py derives the on-disk URL from the manifest's `slug` field; using slug="sobre" for id 185 preserves /sobre/ while slug="about" for id 193 serves /en/about/. translationKey="about" on both keeps them paired in the language switcher exactly as Phase 1 configured.

implementation.approach: Author scripts/content-completion-manifest.json as a JSON array of 5 objects following the shape documented in the outline context (185 slug=sobre/translationKey=about, 193 slug=about/translationKey=about, 226 slug=posts-populares/translationKey=popular-posts, 237 slug=popular-posts/translationKey=popular-posts, 1606 slug=artigos-tech/translationKey=tech-articles). Invoke the existing migrator with `python3 scripts/wp_to_hugo.py --manifest scripts/content-completion-manifest.json --force`; the --force flag (confirmed available by Phase 2.1) is what authorizes overwriting the Phase 1 placeholder about pages and the Phase 2 artigos-tech _index.md. The writer composes each page's URL from the manifest `slug`, so the per-entry slug choice above is what preserves /sobre/ for PT while the EN sibling lives at /en/about/. Finally re-run `hugo --quiet` to prove every page renders cleanly through the live theme.
implementation.verify:
set -euo pipefail
test -f scripts/content-completion-manifest.json
python3 -c "import json; m=json.load(open('scripts/content-completion-manifest.json')); assert len(m)==5, len(m); ids={e['id'] for e in m}; assert ids=={185,193,226,237,1606}, ids; print('manifest ok')"
python3 -m py_compile scripts/wp_to_hugo.py
python3 scripts/wp_to_hugo.py --manifest scripts/content-completion-manifest.json --force
test -f content/pt-br/posts-populares/_index.md
test -f content/en/popular-posts/_index.md
test -f content/pt-br/about/index.md
test -f content/en/about/index.md
test -f content/pt-br/recomendacoes/artigos-tech/_index.md
! grep -q 'Olá — sou o Marcelio' content/pt-br/about/index.md
! grep -q "Hey — I'm Marcelio" content/en/about/index.md
grep -qE '^slug:[[:space:]]*"?sobre"?[[:space:]]*$' content/pt-br/about/index.md
grep -qE 'translationKey:[[:space:]]*"?about"?' content/pt-br/about/index.md
grep -qE 'translationKey:[[:space:]]*"?about"?' content/en/about/index.md
grep -qE 'translationKey:[[:space:]]*"?popular-posts"?' content/pt-br/posts-populares/_index.md
grep -qE 'translationKey:[[:space:]]*"?popular-posts"?' content/en/popular-posts/_index.md
grep -qE 'title:' content/pt-br/about/index.md
grep -qE 'title:' content/en/about/index.md
hugo --quiet
test -f public/sobre/index.html
test -f public/en/about/index.html
test -f public/posts-populares/index.html
test -f public/en/popular-posts/index.html
test -f public/recomendacoes/artigos-tech/index.html

verification.expect: The migrator runs end-to-end against the 5-entry manifest, overwrites every existing placeholder file, creates the two popular-posts bundles, and a full Hugo build renders /sobre/, /en/about/, /posts-populares/, /en/popular-posts/, and /recomendacoes/artigos-tech/ without errors.

tasks: Create scripts/content-completion-manifest.json as a JSON array with the 5 entries for WP ids 185, 193, 226, 237, 1606 using the slug/lang/translationKey/target_path mapping from the approach
Set entry 185 slug to sobre (not about) so wp_to_hugo.py's URL composition keeps the PT about page serving at /sobre/ for URL preservation
Give entries 185 and 193 the same translationKey about so Hugo's language switcher pairs the PT and EN about pages
Give entries 226 and 237 the shared translationKey popular-posts so the PT posts-populares page pairs with the EN popular-posts page
Run python3 -m py_compile scripts/wp_to_hugo.py to confirm the migrator module still parses before invoking it
Invoke python3 scripts/wp_to_hugo.py --manifest scripts/content-completion-manifest.json --force and confirm it exits 0 with the three overwritten and two created files on disk

Confirm the Phase 1 PT placeholder sentence Olá — sou o Marcelio and the Phase 1 EN placeholder sentence Hey — I'm Marcelio no longer appear anywhere under content/pt-br/about/index.md or content/en/about/index.md

Run hugo --quiet from the repo root and verify public/sobre/index.html, public/en/about/index.html, public/posts-populares/index.html, public/en/popular-posts/index.html, and public/recomendacoes/artigos-tech/index.html all exist

userStories.title: Add Popular Posts links to the per-language nav menu
userStories.description: As a bilingual site visitor, I want a Popular Posts link in the header nav of each language so that I can reach the curated list in one click from any page.
acceptanceCriteria: After the site is rebuilt, the rendered PT home page (public/index.html) contains a header nav link to /posts-populares/ labeled "Posts Populares", and the EN home page (public/en/index.html) contains a header nav link to /en/popular-posts/ labeled "Popular Posts" — the existing header.html `{{ range site.Menus.main }}` loop surfaces them with no template change.

hugo.toml declares `[[languages.pt-br.menu.main]]` with `name = "Posts Populares"`, `pageRef = "/posts-populares"`, `weight = 15`, and `[[languages.en.menu.main]]` with `name = "Popular Posts"`, `pageRef = "/popular-posts"`, `weight = 15`, so Popular Posts slots between Sobre/About (weight 10) and Recomendações/Recommendations (weight 20).

hugo.toml remains valid TOML (tomllib.load succeeds) and `hugo --quiet` builds the site clean with the new menu entries (pageRefs resolve to the content pages produced by US-001 with no "REF_NOT_FOUND" error).
`bash -n` on any shell snippet the story adds passes, and `hugo --quiet` exits 0 — the project's own build/syntax check.

implementation.approach: Append two array-of-tables entries to hugo.toml: one `[[languages.pt-br.menu.main]]` block with name="Posts Populares", pageRef="/posts-populares", weight=15 placed after the existing Sobre block (lines 16-19) and before Recomendações (lines 21-24); one `[[languages.en.menu.main]]` block with name="Popular Posts", pageRef="/popular-posts", weight=15 placed after About (lines 32-35) and before Recommendations (lines 37-40). Weight 15 slots Popular Posts between the weight-10 and weight-20 neighbours, keeping the ordering Sobre → Posts Populares → Recomendações (and the English mirror). No change to themes/PaperMod/layouts/partials/header.html — its existing `{{ range site.Menus.main }}` loop surfaces any menu entry declared under the current language.
implementation.verify:
set -e
grep -q 'name = "Posts Populares"' hugo.toml
grep -q 'name = "Popular Posts"' hugo.toml
grep -q 'pageRef = "/posts-populares"' hugo.toml
grep -q 'pageRef = "/popular-posts"' hugo.toml
python3 -c "import tomllib; tomllib.load(open('hugo.toml','rb'))"
rm -rf public && hugo --quiet
grep -Eq 'href="?/posts-populares/"?' public/index.html
grep -Eq 'href="?/en/popular-posts/"?' public/en/index.html

verification.expect: hugo rebuilds cleanly and both rendered language home pages carry a header nav link to their respective Popular Posts page.

tasks: Open hugo.toml and locate the `[[languages.pt-br.menu.main]]` block for Sobre (weight 10) and the one for Recomendações (weight 20).
Insert a new `[[languages.pt-br.menu.main]]` block between them with name="Posts Populares", pageRef="/posts-populares", weight=15.
Locate the `[[languages.en.menu.main]]` blocks for About (weight 10) and Recommendations (weight 20).
Insert a new `[[languages.en.menu.main]]` block between them with name="Popular Posts", pageRef="/popular-posts", weight=15.
Confirm hugo.toml still parses as TOML with `python3 -c "import tomllib; tomllib.load(open('hugo.toml','rb'))"`.
Run `rm -rf public && hugo --quiet` to rebuild the site and confirm no `REF_NOT_FOUND` warnings for the new pageRefs.
Grep public/index.html for the PT nav link to /posts-populares/ and public/en/index.html for the EN nav link to /en/popular-posts/.

userStories.title: Phase 2.2 exit verification: live staging shows real About, Popular Posts navigable, Artigos Tech with content
userStories.description: As the site owner closing Phase 2.2, I want a pre-deploy local smoke check followed by a live verification of the deployed staging URLs so that I can confirm the About bio, Popular Posts listings, and Artigos Tech page render real content with the new nav entries present in both languages.
acceptanceCriteria: Pre-deploy smoke passes locally: hugo --quiet builds without error; content/pt-br/posts-populares/_index.md and content/en/popular-posts/_index.md exist; content/pt-br/about/index.md no longer contains the Phase 1 placeholder 'Olá — sou o Marcelio'; content/en/about/index.md no longer contains the Phase 1 placeholder 'Hey — I'm Marcelio'; hugo.toml declares a nav entry named 'Posts Populares'.

After the commit lands on main, Netlify auto-deploys (wired in Phase 2.1) and reaches state=ready for the new HEAD commit within 3 minutes of the push, observable via the Netlify deploy status for site new.marcelioleal.com.

Live GET https://new.marcelioleal.com/sobre/ returns HTTP 200, body does NOT contain the Phase 1 placeholder 'Olá — sou o Marcelio' (nor its unescaped form 'Olá — sou o Marcelio'), and contains at least one paragraph of Marcelio's real bio text.

Live GET https://new.marcelioleal.com/en/about/ returns HTTP 200, body does NOT contain the Phase 1 placeholder 'Hey — I'm Marcelio' (nor 'Hey — I'm Marcelio'), and contains at least one paragraph of real English bio text.
Live GET https://new.marcelioleal.com/posts-populares/ and https://new.marcelioleal.com/en/popular-posts/ each return HTTP 200 and render list content (non-empty body).

Live GET https://new.marcelioleal.com/recomendacoes/artigos-tech/ returns HTTP 200 and the body differs from the Phase 2 placeholder stub (contains the migrated WordPress article content, not the placeholder sentinel).

Live GET https://new.marcelioleal.com/ body contains a nav link with text 'Posts Populares' pointing at /posts-populares/, and GET https://new.marcelioleal.com/en/ body contains a nav link with text 'Popular Posts' pointing at /en/popular-posts/.

No regression on live staging: robots.txt still serves 'Disallow: /'; response headers on / still include Content-Security-Policy and Strict-Transport-Security; 5 pre-selected sample post URLs (one per language, mixed years) each return HTTP 200.
Visual gate reviewer confirms via the Phase 2.2 prompt that all A-E checks pass, or lists the specific failures that block closing Phase 2.2.
hugo --quiet exits 0 with no build errors or warnings-as-errors.
userStories.notes: Verification-only gate story: implementation.files is intentionally empty. The local pre-deploy smoke runs in implementation.verify; the live post-deploy checks are enumerated as acceptanceCriteria and confirmed through the visual gate because the Netlify deploy wait and live curl loop are human-observable and consume criteria that no single local command executes. Sample post URLs for the no-regression check should be chosen at execute time from the 5 most-recently-migrated posts (pick before pushing).

implementation.approach: Pre-deploy: run the local smoke (hugo build + file-existence + placeholder-absence greps + nav-entry grep) via implementation.verify to prove the tree is ready to ship. Then commit and push to main; Netlify's Phase 2.1 wiring triggers an auto-deploy. Poll the Netlify deploy status (via the Netlify CLI or API for site new.marcelioleal.com) until state=ready for the pushed commit, max 3 minutes. Then run the live curl loop described in acceptanceCriteria against new.marcelioleal.com, including HTTP 200 checks, placeholder-string negations on /sobre/ and /en/about/, body-content assertions for /posts-populares/, /en/popular-posts/ and /recomendacoes/artigos-tech/, nav-link assertions on / and /en/, and the no-regression sweep (robots.txt, CSP/HSTS headers, 5 sample post URLs). Close the visual gate with the Phase 2.2 prompt once every check reports pass.
implementation.verify: set -euo pipefail; hugo --quiet; test -f content/pt-br/posts-populares/_index.md; test -f content/en/popular-posts/_index.md; ! grep -q 'Olá — sou o Marcelio' content/pt-br/about/index.md; ! grep -q "Hey — I'm Marcelio" content/en/about/index.md; grep -q 'name = "Posts Populares"' hugo.toml; grep -q 'Marcelio' content/pt-br/about/index.md; grep -q 'Marcelio' content/en/about/index.md

verification.expect: Live staging: /sobre/ and /en/about/ show the real bio (no Phase 1 placeholder); /posts-populares/ and /en/popular-posts/ are navigable and render list content; /recomendacoes/artigos-tech/ shows the migrated WordPress content (not the Phase 2 stub); the PT nav shows 'Posts Populares' and the EN nav shows 'Popular Posts'; robots.txt still serves Disallow:/, CSP/HSTS headers intact, 5 sample post URLs return 200.

gate.prompt: Phase 2.2 live verify: /sobre/ and /en/about/ show the real bio (not placeholders), /posts-populares/ and /en/popular-posts/ are navigable, /recomendacoes/artigos-tech/ loads real content. Nav shows the new entries on both languages. OK to close Phase 2.2?

tasks: Run hugo --quiet locally and confirm the build completes with no errors
Confirm content/pt-br/posts-populares/_index.md and content/en/popular-posts/_index.md both exist on disk
Grep content/pt-br/about/index.md and content/en/about/index.md to confirm no Phase 1 placeholder strings remain
Grep hugo.toml to confirm the 'Posts Populares' nav entry is declared
Commit the Phase 2.2 changes with a descriptive subject and push to main
Poll Netlify deploy status for new.marcelioleal.com until state=ready for the pushed commit (max 3 min)
curl https://new.marcelioleal.com/sobre/ and assert 200 + no Phase 1 placeholder + real bio paragraph present
curl https://new.marcelioleal.com/en/about/ and assert 200 + no English placeholder + real bio paragraph present
curl /posts-populares/ and /en/popular-posts/ and assert 200 with non-empty list body on both
curl /recomendecoes/artigos-tech/ and assert 200 + body differs from the Phase 2 placeholder stub
curl / and /en/ homepages and assert the PT nav has 'Posts Populares' and the EN nav has 'Popular Posts'
Fetch robots.txt + response headers on / and verify Disallow:/ still served and CSP/HSTS headers intact
Pick 5 sample post URLs and curl each, confirming HTTP 200 on all 5 (no regression)
Record each check's pass/fail outcome and resolve the visual gate with either 'All A-E pass' or 'Blocked — list failures'
